name: False wage reporting to tax and social-insurance systems

attribution.legal_posture: Post-sentence official summary. Chapman’s plea and sentence are adjudicated; aggregate worker conduct is agency-reported, while unnamed-worker adjudication remains outside the summary.

caveats: Christina Chapman's conviction is adjudicated; the agency's aggregate description leaves every unnamed worker and identity-theft event at the reporting stage.
Keep stolen identity names, taxpayer identifiers, forms, and company identities out of publication.
Payroll and tax reporting belongs in organizational control and victim-remediation review; inconsistent records require corroboration before worker attribution.
Preserve the distinction between Chapman’s conviction and the report's aggregate description of unnamed workers.

infrastructure.statement: IRS-CI reports that much of the $17.1 million generated in the Chapman scheme was falsely reported as wages to the IRS and Social Security Administration under stolen or borrowed U.S. identities. This establishes a tax-and-payroll harm pathway in addition to hiring deception and laptop hosting.

sources.support: Publication 3583 is marked Rev. 3-2026; month precision only is supported, so no exact March publication day is asserted. IRS-CI states that much of the scheme's $17.1 million was reported as wages under the names of U.S. people whose identities had been stolen or borrowed. It records Chapman's guilty plea, 102-month sentence, forfeiture order and monetary judgment
sources.locator: ‘North Korean Information Technology Scheme,’ PDF page 6 / printed pp. 8-9
